items.title: $NLST When NLST came out with HyperCloud in 2009, it made such a splash that the stock rose from $1 to $8 in eight trading days. It was due
items.content_excerpt: $NLST When NLST came out with HyperCloud in 2009, it made such a splash that the stock rose from $1 to $8 in eight trading days. It was due to 2 technologies that NLST invented called "rank-multiplication” and “load-reduction”; RM fooled the processor into using more DRAM; kinda like how VMWare fooled the server into create many virtual servers. The technology was so important that it was stolen by Samsung, Micron and Hynix……and especially by Google who was developing their own architecture. Now that we’ve settled with some of those infringers, that very same technology is now used to create two ranks simultaneously to feed data to the CPU; it’s called multiplexed-ranked DIMMs; the world’s fastest & are growing quickly due their their speed/bandwidth. Chuck believes that MRDIMMs will replace RDIMMs; especially if they use LPDDR (low-power)….. as NLST will be the 1st to do. If you doubt what is happening in that space….just look at AMD’s new offering with MRDIMMs https://wccftech.com/amd-zen-6-architecture-ipc-cores-memory-performance-epyc-venice/

items.title: $NLST This is the first time in a long time that Chuck has focused on Hybrid CXL (formerly HyperVault, then HybriDimm, and also Storage Clas
items.content_excerpt: $NLST This is the first time in a long time that Chuck has focused on Hybrid CXL (formerly HyperVault, then HybriDimm, and also Storage Class Memory). It is interesting to see him excited about the potential of this technology in the AI era. They have been working on it for many years and now see an opportunity to get this product into the marketplace via KV Cache. Originally set to replace DIMMs, it will now be in the tier above SSD’s in the KV Cache hierarchy at nearly the speed of DRAM with the capacity of SSD’s. Long-context LLMs create large memory demands on KV cache. Current systems store the full cache in host memory but that quickly hits a ceiling: when context length grows, the volume of KV transfers rises and becomes the primary source of latency. The Hybrid CXL is built for KV Cache with their patented “prefetch" and “Terabytes" of memory; the ultimate solution for the LLM long-context problem. Hong: "It is certainly past the research stages and its in full development."

It does NOT mean Samsung still owes Netlist that cash! The money is already in Netlist's hands. Only its accounting recognition is spread over time. Just accounting rules! 😂 Sources: SEC Form 10-Q, Q3 2026 — Note 1, Revenue Recognition and Contract Assets and Liabilities; MD&A, Net Sales. https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1282631/000110465926125311/nlst-20260926x10q.htm Netlist Q3 earnings release: https://investors.netlist.com/news/netlist-reports-third-quarter-2026-results/4b0b1c7b-4a86-40a8-b57e-6fb5f30c5124

items.title: $NLST 1/2 THE SAMSUNG $200 MILLION ACCOUNTING MAGIC! 🪄💰 There seems to be some confusion between CASH RECEIVED and REVENUE RECOGNIZED. Netli
items.content_excerpt: $NLST 1/2 THE SAMSUNG $200 MILLION ACCOUNTING MAGIC! 🪄💰 There seems to be some confusion between CASH RECEIVED and REVENUE RECOGNIZED. Netlist has ALREADY RECEIVED the full $200 million upfront payment from Samsung, plus the first $27.5 million quarterly payment. That's $227.5 MILLION in actual cash received during Q3 2026. So why does the income statement show only $44.9 million in Samsung license revenue? Because under ASC 606, the upfront license payment is recognized as revenue over the 20-quarter (five-year) license term, since Samsung receives ongoing access to Netlist's patent portfolio, including future additions. The Q3 breakdown is: - $200M upfront cash: ALREADY RECEIVED. - $27.5M first quarterly cash payment: ALREADY RECEIVED. - $12.0M: Q3 recognition of the upfront license fee, including Korean withholding taxes. - $32.9M: Q3 recognition of the first quarterly license fee, including those taxes. - $44.9M: total Samsung license revenue recognized in Q3.

items.content_excerpt: $CAPR Valuation Math • Earnings Trajectory: Modeling $6.00 EPS in FY 2027 and $14.00 EPS in FY 2028 on a solo U.S. launch, 65 mil shares, Fully Taxed at 700k/patient/year scaling toward 2,500 patients on Floor 2 capacity. • Unrisked Present Value: Put a standard 10x to 15x rare-disease P/E multiple on 2028's $14.00 EPS ($140–$210). items.content_excerpt: $VG Thinking a 1.75M share block at the exact close is just an "MM closing a daily grift" shows a total misunderstanding of institutional order flow. That is a classic Market-On-Close (MOC) block trades. Large institutions and index funds use MOC orders to accumulate massive positions at the official closing price to minimize market impact and tracking error. An MM doesn’t just casually conjure up multi-million share buying demand out of thin air to cover a day trade—they are facilitating massive institutional accumulation. Smart money is quietly absorbing the float right under everyone's noses at a dirt-cheap 8.7x P/E while retail screams manipulation. Watch the volume, not the noise.

$NLST This is the first time in a long time that Chuck has focused on Hybrid CXL (formerly HyperVault, then HybriDimm, and also Storage Class Memory). It is interesting to see him excited about the potential of this technology in the AI era. They have been working on it for many years and now see an opportunity to get this product into the marketplace via KV Cache. Originally set to replace DIMMs, it will now be in the tier above SSD’s in the KV Cache hierarchy at nearly the speed of DRAM with the capacity of SSD’s. Long-context LLMs create large memory demands on KV cache. Current systems store the full cache in host memory but that quickly hits a ceiling: when context length grows, the volume of KV transfers rises and becomes the primary source of latency. The Hybrid CXL is built for KV Cache with their patented “prefetch" and “Terabytes" of memory; the ultimate solution for the LLM long-context problem. Hong: "It is certainly past the research stages and its in full development."

$NLST 1/2 THE SAMSUNG $200 MILLION ACCOUNTING MAGIC! 🪄💰 There seems to be some confusion between CASH RECEIVED and REVENUE RECOGNIZED. Netlist has ALREADY RECEIVED the full $200 million upfront payment from Samsung, plus the first $27.5 million quarterly payment. That's $227.5 MILLION in actual cash received during Q3 2026. So why does the income statement show only $44.9 million in Samsung license revenue? Because under ASC 606, the upfront license payment is recognized as revenue over the 20-quarter (five-year) license term, since Samsung receives ongoing access to Netlist's patent portfolio, including future additions. The Q3 breakdown is: - $200M upfront cash: ALREADY RECEIVED. - $27.5M first quarterly cash payment: ALREADY RECEIVED. - $12.0M: Q3 recognition of the upfront license fee, including Korean withholding taxes. - $32.9M: Q3 recognition of the first quarterly license fee, including those taxes. - $44.9M: total Samsung license revenue recognized in Q3.
